question: A 72-year-old man comes to the physician because of fatigue and a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss over the past 6 months despite a good appetite. He takes no medications. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Physical examination shows hepatosplenomegaly and diffuse, nontender lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin concentration of 11 g/dL and a leukocyte count of 16,000/mm3. A direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test is positive. A photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Positive direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test -> autoimmune hemolytic anemia -> hemoglobin concentration of 11 g/dL -> 80% CHAIN: Hepatosplenomegaly and diffuse, nontender lymphadenopathy -> lymphoproliferative disorder -> leukocyte count of 16,000/mm3 -> 75% CHAIN: Weight loss despite good appetite -> hypermetabolic state -> possible malignancy -> 70% CHAIN: Photomicrograph of peripheral blood smear showing atypical lymphocytes -> lymphoproliferative disorder -> possible lymphoma or leukemia -> 60% CHAIN: Clinical presentation of fatigue, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, and lymphadenopathy -> systemic illness -> 50% CHAIN: Overall clinical picture suggests a hematologic malignancy -> possible leukemia or lymphoma -> 80%
analysis: The presentation of fatigue, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, anemia, leukocytosis, and a positive Coombs test suggests a hematologic malignancy. The photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear would likely show atypical lymphocytes. Given the age of the patient and the findings, the most likely diagnosis is Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).
